rules.name: Google Crawling Infrastructure: HTTP status codes

description.en: Links on the page lead to an error page. People who follow them hit a dead end, and search engines drop such addresses from their index.
description.uk: Посилання на сторінці ведуть на сторінку помилки. Люди, які переходять за ними, потрапляють у глухий кут, а пошукові системи вилучають такі адреси зі свого індексу.

rule.quote: In the case of Google Search, Google doesn't index URLs that return a 4xx status code, and URLs that are already indexed and return a 4xx status code are removed from the index.

source.name: Google Crawling Infrastructure: HTTP status codes

fixDirection.en: Update or remove hrefs that return 4xx or 5xx; 301 moved targets to their new URL.
fixDirection.uk: Оновіть або приберіть href, що повертають 4xx чи 5xx; для перенесених цілей налаштуйте 301 на нову адресу.

rules.name: Google Search Central: introduction to structured data
Google Search Central: software app structured data

description.en: Structured data on the page leaves out properties that Google lists as required for its type. Without them the markup is not eligible for the rich result it was written for.
description.uk: Структуровані дані на сторінці пропускають властивості, які Google називає обов’язковими для цього типу. Без них розмітка не може дати розширеного результату, заради якого її написали.

rule.quote: You must include all the required properties for an object to be eligible for appearance in Google Search with enhanced display.

source.name: Google Search Central: introduction to structured data

fixDirection.en: Add each listed required property as the type's Google page names it, then re-test.
fixDirection.uk: Додайте кожну названу обов’язкову властивість так, як її описує сторінка Google для цього типу, і перевірте знову.

rules.name: This skill: the Vectorscope reading (h2 sections, 2,000-character windows, a 26-passage cap)

description.en: Some passages begin in the middle of a sentence, because a long section was cut into pieces. Read on its own, such a passage makes little sense, and AI answers quote passages on their own.
description.uk: Деякі уривки починаються з середини речення, бо довгий розділ розрізали на частини. Окремо такий уривок мало що означає, а ШІ-відповіді цитують уривки саме окремо.

text.en: The Vectorscope reading cuts the kept text at h2 sections, then into 2,000-character windows; a passage that opens inside a sentence is flagged. This is this skill's rule.
text.uk: Читання Vectorscope ріже збережений текст за розділами h2, а потім на вікна по 2 000 символів; уривок, що відкривається всередині речення, позначається. Це правило цієї навички.

fixDirection.en: Break long sections with more h2 or h3 headings so that cuts fall at headings; keep sections under about 2,000 characters.
fixDirection.uk: Розбийте довгі розділи додатковими заголовками h2 чи h3, щоб розрізи припадали на заголовки; тримайте розділи коротшими за приблизно 2 000 символів.

label.en: No answer: “Can I paste a link to a PDF instead o…”
label.uk: Без відповіді: “Can I paste a link to a PDF instead o…”

evidence.question: Can I paste a link to a PDF instead of a web page?

rules.name: Google Search Central: AI features and your website
This skill's rule (README, the thresholds)

description.en: A question people would ask about this topic has no answer anywhere in the page's passages. An assistant asked it has nothing on this page to quote, so it answers from somewhere else.
description.uk: Запитання, яке люди поставили б на цю тему, не має відповіді в жодному уривку сторінки. Асистент, якого про це спитають, не має на цій сторінці що цитувати, тож відповідає з іншого джерела.

text.en: The agent writes the questions people ask and judges each against the passages; one that no passage answers is flagged. The questions and verdicts are the agent's judgement, and the quote is checked against the passage.
text.uk: Агент пише запитання, які ставлять люди, і оцінює кожне за уривками; запитання, на яке не відповідає жоден уривок, позначається. Запитання й вердикти — судження агента, а цитату перевіряють за уривком.

fixDirection.en: Add a passage, ideally under its own h2 or h3, that answers the question directly in its first two sentences.
fixDirection.uk: Додайте уривок, бажано під власним h2 чи h3, що прямо відповідає на запитання в перших двох реченнях.

rules.name: HTML Standard: the nav element
This skill: the Vectorscope reading (h2 sections, 2,000-character windows, a 26-passage cap)

description.en: A run of short, menu-like lines sits inside the main text. AI readers keep it as content, and it breaks up the passage around it.
description.uk: Низка коротких рядків, схожих на меню, стоїть усередині основного тексту. ШІ-читачі зберігають її як вміст, і вона розриває уривок навколо себе.

rule.quote: The nav element represents a section of a page that links to other pages or to parts within the page: a section with navigation links.

fixDirection.en: Wrap link lists in <nav> (or <aside>) outside the main text flow.
fixDirection.uk: Обгорніть списки посилань у <nav> (або <aside>) поза основним потоком тексту.

description.en: The model does not know the brand at all. An assistant answering from memory cannot describe it and depends entirely on what it can find and read.
description.uk: Модель зовсім не знає бренду. Асистент, що відповідає з пам’яті, не може його описати й цілком залежить від того, що зможе знайти й прочитати.

text.en: When all five of the model's answers say it does not know the brand, the brand is unknown to that model. One model's judgement; fixed rules from Brandscope.
text.uk: Коли всі п’ять відповідей моделі кажуть, що вона не знає бренду, бренд цій моделі невідомий. Судження однієї моделі; фіксовані правила з Brandscope.

fixDirection.en: Make the basics explicit on key pages (what it is, for whom, the price) and earn mentions on independent sources.
fixDirection.uk: Чітко викладіть основне на ключових сторінках (що це, для кого, ціна) і здобувайте згадки в незалежних джерелах.

rules.name: This skill's rule (README, the thresholds)

description.en: The page's HTML is very large, or it loads many scripts. All of it has to be downloaded and parsed before the text is ready, which is slow on phones and costly for crawlers.
description.uk: HTML сторінки дуже великий або вона завантажує багато скриптів. Усе це треба завантажити й розібрати, перш ніж текст буде готовий, а це повільно на телефонах і дорого для краулерів.

text.en: HTML over 500 KB, or more than 30 scripts, is a heavy page. The threshold is this skill's; speed for real visitors is what Core Web Vitals measure, and this check does not read them.
text.uk: HTML понад 500 КБ або понад 30 скриптів — важка сторінка. Поріг — цієї навички; швидкість для реальних відвідувачів вимірюють Core Web Vitals, і ця перевірка їх не читає.

fixDirection.en: Cut inline JSON, SVG and CSS bulk; defer, async or drop scripts; lazy-load widgets below the fold.
fixDirection.uk: Зменште вбудовані JSON, SVG і CSS; застосуйте defer чи async або приберіть скрипти; віджети нижче першого екрана завантажуйте ліниво.

rules.name: The llms.txt proposal

description.en: The site's llms.txt points only to pages in one language, though this page has other language versions. Agents that start from llms.txt see the site in one language.
description.uk: llms.txt сайту вказує лише на сторінки однією мовою, хоча ця сторінка має інші мовні версії. Агенти, що починають з llms.txt, бачать сайт однією мовою.

text.en: On a site with several language versions, llms.txt is expected to point to more than one of them. The llms.txt proposal says nothing about languages; this is this skill's rule.
text.uk: На сайті з кількома мовними версіями llms.txt має вказувати більше ніж на одну з них. Пропозиція llms.txt нічого не каже про мови; це правило цієї навички.

fixDirection.en: List each language's key pages in llms.txt, or publish one llms.txt per locale and link them.
fixDirection.uk: Перелічіть у llms.txt ключові сторінки кожної мови або опублікуйте окремий llms.txt для кожної локалі й пов’яжіть їх.

rules.name: MDN: CSP frame-ancestors
MDN: X-Content-Type-Options
MDN: Referrer-Policy

description.en: The answer lacks one or more common security headers: framing control, X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy. This does not hide the page from search; it leaves the browser's protections at their defaults.
description.uk: Відповідь не має одного чи кількох поширених заголовків безпеки: контролю вбудовування у фрейми, X-Content-Type-Options чи Referrer-Policy. Від пошуку це сторінку не ховає; захист браузера лишається на типових налаштуваннях.

rule.quote: The header allows you to avoid MIME type sniffing by specifying that the MIME types are deliberately configured.

fixDirection.en: Send Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (or X-Frame-Options), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and a Referrer-Policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin.
fixDirection.uk: Надсилайте Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (або X-Frame-Options), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff і Referrer-Policy, наприклад strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

rules.name: Google Search Central: creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
This skill's rule (README, the thresholds)

description.en: The page has no link to an About or a Contact page. Readers and search engines look for who stands behind a site, and these pages are where they find it.
description.uk: Сторінка не має посилання на сторінку «Про нас» чи «Контакти». Читачі й пошукові системи шукають, хто стоїть за сайтом, і саме там це знаходять.

rule.quote: background about the author or the site that publishes it, such as through links to an author page or a site's About page

source.name: Google Search Central: creating helpful, reliable, people-first content

fixDirection.en: Link About and Contact from the header or the footer of every page.
fixDirection.uk: Додайте посилання «Про нас» і «Контакти» в шапку або підвал кожної сторінки.

passages.heading: What does this mean?

passages.heading: How to read your result
passages.head: Four readings decide whether a page is legible to a retrieval system. Here is what each on
passages.text: Four readings decide whether a page is legible to a retrieval system. Here is what each one means when it is bad. Chunks that never reach the index A retrieval system reads a fixed number of passages from a page and ignores the rest, so anything below that cut is invisible no matter how good it is. Vectorscope applies the same cap the product applies and names the passages that fell outside it. If your answer, your differentiator or your FAQ sits below the cut, the fix is not more words, and semantic chunking will not rescue it either: a well-cut passage past the cap is still a passage nobody reads. Move that passage up, or split the page so it has a passage budget of its own. The extraction ratio The extraction ratio is how much of the page turned into readable text — a low one means most of what you shipped was navigation, boilerplate or markup that no model will ever see. A long page with a low ratio is a short page as far as retrieval is concerned. Extraction happens before any chunking, semantic chunking included, so text lost here is lost to every strategy. Common causes, in the order we see them: text rendered only by JavaScript, an article wrapped in so much chrome that the body is a minority of the document, and images carrying words that exist nowhere in the HTML. Groups, and what a tight group means Groups are the semantic part of this reading, the nearest it comes to semantic chunking: passages the embedding places close together in meaning, whatever heading they sit under. One enormous group usually means the page says one thing many times, which reads as thin to a retriever even when it reads as thorough to an editor. Several small groups with one passage each is the opposite problem: a page that changes subject constantly gives a retriever nothing complete to quote. The passage a question actually retrieves Asking the page a question returns the passages that answer it, ranked, using only that page — which is the closest thing to watching a model

passages.head: to quote. The passage a question actually retrieves Asking the page a question returns the
passages.text: to quote. The passage a question actually retrieves Asking the page a question returns the passages that answer it, ranked, using only that page — which is the closest thing to watching a model decide what your page is for. If the returned passage is not the one you would have chosen, the page is not organised the way you think it is. This is also the fastest way to test a heading rewrite: change the heading, run the page again, ask the same question.

passages.heading: What is semantic chunking?
passages.head: Semantic chunking is splitting a page into passages where its meaning changes, instead of
passages.text: Semantic chunking is splitting a page into passages where its meaning changes, instead of every fixed number of characters or at every heading. Vectorscope does not cut that way: it cuts at each h2 and then in fixed windows, and its semantic step comes after the cut, when the passages are grouped by meaning. 01 Fixed-length chunking Fixed-length chunking cuts every N characters and is the default in most pipelines because it is trivial to implement. It also cuts through the middle of a sentence, separates a heading from the answer under it, and produces passages that begin with half a word. Vectorscope uses it only inside a long section: a window of 2,000 characters with 200 characters of overlap, ending at a sentence break where one is close enough. 02 Heading-aware chunking Heading-aware chunking uses the page's own headings as the cut lines, so a passage arrives with the heading that names it. This is Vectorscope's first cut, and only an h2 makes one: an h3 stays inside the passage of the h2 above it, so a section of six h3 questions is one passage, or several windows of one. It also means your heading text is doing retrieval work. A section called "Overview" contributes nothing to the passage; a section called "Can I cancel at any time?" contributes the question itself. 03 Semantic chunking, and how it differs from grouping Semantic chunking compares neighbouring sentences and cuts where the meaning shifts, which gives passages that stand alone but needs an embedding pass over the page before a single chunk exists. Vectorscope does not do that step. Its semantic part is the grouping: every passage is embedded once it is cut, and passages that sit close in meaning are drawn as one group. So the map asks the question semantic chunking asks — where does one idea end? — of the passages your headings already made. A group spanning three h2 sections says the headings split one idea; a long section whose windows land in two groups says a single heading holds two.

passages.heading: Is my content ready for AI search?
passages.head: This page answers that question for one URL at a time, honestly, which means naming what i
passages.text: This page answers that question for one URL at a time, honestly, which means naming what it cannot see as clearly as what it can. What this tool can tell you How much of your page becomes readable text at all, as a ratio and not an adjective. Exactly which passages a retriever would receive, in order, with the ones beyond the cap marked. Which passages share a subject once they are grouped by meaning — the question semantic chunking asks, put to your own page. Whether your passages stand alone, or lean on the passage before them to make sense. Which passage a real question retrieves from your page, using the page's own embeddings. Whether the page asks to be left out of an index at all — a noindex directive is reported rather than ignored. What it cannot tell you Whether any specific assistant has your page in its index. Nobody outside those companies can see that. How a model ranks your page against a competitor's. That needs a corpus of both, which is the product rather than the demo. Whether you are cited in an answer today. That is a measurement over time on prompts you choose, not a property of one page.

passages.heading: Using Vectorscope to test a RAG pipeline
passages.head: If you build retrieval rather than content, this page is a reference implementation you ca
passages.text: If you build retrieval rather than content, this page is a reference implementation you can point at any URL in about twenty seconds. 1 Run a page you already index, and compare the passage boundaries with your own chunker's — fixed windows, headings or semantic chunking. 2 Note the extraction ratio: if yours is lower on the same URL, your extractor is discarding body text, not boilerplate. 3 Ask the page a question you know the answer to, and check whether the top passage is the one that contains it. 4 Run a page that is far too long. The passages beyond the cap are the ones your own top-k will also never reach. The chunker (h2 cuts, then 2,000-character windows with 200 of overlap), the embedding model and the cap here are the ones the product runs in production. A demo using a simplified pipeline would flatter the pipeline it exists to demonstrate.

passages.heading: Who is Vectorscope for?
passages.head: Vectorscope is for anyone whose page has to be read in passages: the people who write it,
passages.text: Vectorscope is for anyone whose page has to be read in passages: the people who write it, and the people who build the retrieval that reads it. Both get the same reading — the cut, the cap, and the semantic chunking question of which passages belong together. Content and SEO teams For checking that the answer a page exists to give survives into one passage a retriever can quote, above the cap, under a heading that names it. Engineers building RAG For a reference reading of any URL to hold your own chunker against, whether it cuts on fixed windows, headings or semantic chunking. Editors restructuring a page For deciding where a heading belongs: the groups show which sections share a subject and which section is really two. Once the passages are right, the words inside them are next: PatternScope reads a draft for the stock phrases and repeated sentence shapes a reader reacts to.

passages.heading: Words used on this page
passages.head: The terms this page relies on, each defined once, because a page that uses them without de
passages.text: The terms this page relies on, each defined once, because a page that uses them without defining them is a page an assistant cannot explain to anybody. Semantic chunking Cutting text into passages where its meaning changes, rather than at a fixed length or at a heading. On this page the meaning-based step is the grouping of passages that are already cut, not the cut itself. Chunk A passage of a page, cut so it can be read on its own. Retrieval systems store and return chunks, never whole pages, which is why a page's structure matters more than its length. Embedding A list of numbers that stands for the meaning of a passage, so that two passages about the same thing sit near each other. Comparing embeddings is how a retriever finds a passage without matching words. Cosine similarity A measure of how close two embeddings point in the same direction, from 1 for identical to 0 for unrelated. It is the number behind every claim that two passages are about the same thing. Retrieval-augmented generation Answering a question by first retrieving passages from a source and then writing from them, rather than from the model's memory alone. Every AI answer that cites a page did this, and the page it cited was a chunk. Extraction Turning a fetched HTML document into the readable text a model receives, discarding navigation, scripts and boilerplate. What extraction drops, no model ever sees.

passages.heading: Questions people ask about this
passages.head: How does AI Mode choose which sources to cite? Nobody outside Google can state the mechani
passages.text: How does AI Mode choose which sources to cite? Nobody outside Google can state the mechanism, and this page will not pretend to. What is observable is that cited pages tend to contain a passage that answers the query completely on its own, and that pages whose answer is spread across several sections are cited less often than their content deserves. Vectorscope shows you whether your page has such a passage. How do I get cited in AI Overviews? Give the answer its own passage, under a heading that names the question, high enough on the page to survive the retrieval cap. That is not a trick — it is the shape retrieval rewards, and you can check whether your page has it by running it here. Is this an embedding visualization tool? Yes, for one page at a time. It embeds every passage of a URL and groups them by meaning, so you can see which parts of the page are near each other and which stand alone. It does not plot a corpus of thousands of documents. What is the difference between heading-aware and semantic chunking? Heading-aware chunking cuts at the page's own headings; semantic chunking cuts where the meaning changes, whether or not there is a heading there. The first is cheap and follows the author; the second needs every sentence embedded before a single cut is made. Does Vectorscope use semantic chunking? Not to cut the page. Vectorscope cuts at every h2 — an h3 does not start a passage — and splits a long section into 2,000-character windows with 200 characters of overlap. The semantic step comes after: each passage is embedded and passages close in meaning are grouped, which shows where semantic chunking would disagree with your headings. Do you store the page I test? The reading is kept briefly so it can be shared with a link, and the fetched page itself is not retained after the reading is produced. No account is needed, so there is nothing to attach it to. passages.heading: Other free AI search tools
passages.head: Voicescope Start with one keyword and explore the questions a person may ask an AI assista
passages.text: Voicescope Start with one keyword and explore the questions a person may ask an AI assistant across real-life contexts. Brandscope Ask three AI assistants the buyer questions around a brand, then compare their answers with the brand's own page. Reviewscope Ask three AI assistants what reviews say about a brand — first without naming a platform, then naming all twelve — and see which ratings they state without a source. PatternScope Paste a page to see the stock phrases, repeated sentence shapes and unchecked claims a reader reacts to. Not an AI detector. AI answer volatility A daily reading of how far AI assistants' answers moved since yesterday, so a drop in your own visibility can be read against the day it happened on. All free tools
